name: Jeiel
overview: Jeiel is a male biblical figure identified specifically as the son of Hotham the Aroerite. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide further details about his tribal affiliation or additional notes. His mention is concise, grounding his identity primarily in his paternal lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeiel means 'G-d has preserved' or possibly 'G-d sweeps up,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's active role. This proper name is found in 1 Chronicles 11:44 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Jeiel is explicitly recorded as the son of Hotham, identified as the Aroerite. Scripture does not document any other family relationships for Jeiel beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jeiel's significance in the biblical record lies in his identification as a descendant of Hotham the Aroerite, situating him within the post-exilic genealogical framework of Israel. His mention in 1 Chronicles 11:44 contributes to the historical and tribal listings that affirm the continuity of God's people. Though brief, his inclusion underscores the importance of preserving genealogical records in the biblical narrative.
